conclusion: Under the assumed costs, going from 1 to 10 subscribers raised direct publisher time per event 10x (1.8 to 18 ms) and the assumed pub/sub publish cost 1.35x (0.052 to 0.07 ms, small but growing with fan-out); with one 50 ms subscriber the simulated fast subscribers waited 31483.88 ms on average with direct calls versus 1.87 ms with pub/sub, and the slow subscriber kept its own work but overlapped it with the others, finishing at 51511.67 ms instead of 67960.95 ms while its queue grew to 902 events.
setup: virtual-time simulation (costs assumed, queueing derived), 1000 order-placed events arriving every 5 ms, subscribers 1/3/10, fast work 1-2 ms, one slow subscriber +50 ms, direct call RTT 0.3 ms, topic publish 0.05 ms + 0.002 ms per queue, delivery 0.3 ms, seed 61
